approaches.title: Greedy largest-coin selection
approaches.summary: Sorts coins and repeatedly chooses the largest coin that does not exceed the remaining amount. This strategy is marked incorrect because greedy choices do not always produce the minimum number of coins.

revisions.commitComment: why do i keep making this mistake
revisions.rawCommitSubject: rust 322!: why do i keep making this mistake
revisions.shortChangeSummary: Introduces a descending-style greedy process that repeatedly subtracts the largest usable coin. Marked wrong because this does not guarantee an optimal solution.

approaches.title: Depth-first search
approaches.summary: Recursively explores coin choices until reaching the target amount, returning the first successful combination found. Sorting changes traversal order but does not guarantee a minimum-length solution, and this revision is marked incorrect.

revisions.commitComment: no memo yet, but algo performs dfs which even with sorting doesn't gurantee best case
revisions.rawCommitSubject: rust 322!: no memo yet, but algo performs dfs which even with sorting doesn't gurantee best case
revisions.shortChangeSummary: Replaces greedy subtraction with recursive depth-first exploration of coin combinations. It returns the first feasible result without memoization or minimum tracking, so it is marked wrong.

approaches.title: Breadth-first search
approaches.summary: Treats each remaining amount as a graph state and explores all states level by level. The first reached zero uses the fewest coins, while a hash set prevents revisiting states.

revisions.shortChangeSummary: Replaces recursive DFS with breadth-first exploration of remaining amounts and tracks visited states. Returning the depth at which zero is reached yields the minimum coin count.
